newsitem.title: JAPAN: EC's Santer slaps U.S. Helms-Burton Act.
newsitem.headline: EC's Santer slaps U.S. Helms-Burton Act.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer on Thursday said Europe could not accept Washington's anti-Cuba laws, which Brussels has said it plans to challenge at the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

"I have to say that we cannot accept the extra-territorial dimension of the Helms-Burton Act...," Santer told Reuters in an interview. "Europe is not the only one to oppose this. Canada, Mexico and others are also backing our position."
European Union foreign ministers decided on Tuesday to request a dispute panel at a WTO meeting in Geneva on October 16, challenging the U.S. law passed in July.
"I think that we have to use all the possibilities, such as dispute settlement of the WTO, to convince our market partner that they cannot go in this direction," Santer added.
U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Tuesday that the EU's move "unnecessarily escalates tensions".
The Helms-Burton law aims to curb foreign investment in Cuba by penalising companies doing business in the Communist-ruled island.
